title: The queue-file check surface, the last two queue columns, the member sheet, the cap limit key, the finding codes, the right of the load and the decision code are not specified in the sources
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-014); Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3 (A2.3, A2.17, AC-P4-003-01, AC-ALT-P4-003-02, AC-EXC-P4-003-01); Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3 (T6.1, T6.2, appendix T-A.1); P4 context pack (service row, ownership rows); ASM-A6-api-4
description: (a) The P4 ownership rows name five tables (delegation_limit, masking_rule, permission, role, role_conflict) and none is a queue, and the reference-load family of TSD P4 appendix T-A.1 (API-P4-005, API-P4-006, API-P4-009, API-P4-010) belongs to rwb-case under ASM-A6-api-4, so the queue rows, the member rows and the reference load are P3's and no source names the check that stands in front of them; (b) the two operations of this story (POST and GET /admin/queue-file-checks) therefore have no source path and no source schema, and the exact path and shape of the five consumed owner operations are not in the documents read for this WP; (c) the legacy Data table gives the queue as id, queue_code, queue_name, team_code, role_code, assignment_method and 2 more, so the names of DF-WRK-007 and DF-WRK-008 are not stated - they are read here as capacity_cap and overflow_queue_code from FSD AC-ALT-P4-003-02 and legacy AC2; (d) the legacy story lists a queue file but no member sheet, while FSD AC-P4-003-01 loads a QUEUE_MEMBER sheet of 48 rows, so whether the gate inspects members is unfixed; (e) the caseload cap maximum is a parameter (DL23) and no source names its key, its value or its unit; (f) the seven finding codes and their field names are not source values; (g) the legacy Permission checks table gives the load Rules and parameters R and the approval Rules and parameters A to RW-RISK while TSD P4 T6.1 carries the same letters in Reference data (RW-COE and RW-REFADM hold C) and grants no A holder there, so the right of the load, and the difference between the two tables, are unfixed; (h) the decision code and the case id of the acceptance entry of DP-03 are not stated; (i) the legacy Endpoints table lists the rule-version read and the rule-version approve, which are RWB-AD-011 and RWB-AD-012, on the monolith base /api/recovery/v1/.
evidence: P4 context pack tables (5 owned tables; 4 REST operations provided: GET /admin/access-log, GET /admin/roles, GET /me/session, POST /admin/break-glass-grants); TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 (API-P4-005 to API-P4-010), T6.1 (42 role rows, three capability columns); FSD P4 v3 A2.3 field catalog and AC-P4-003-01, AC-ALT-P4-003-02, AC-EXC-P4-003-01; legacy RWB-AD-014 Data, Endpoints, Permission checks and Test cases tables; ASM-A6-api-4.
proposed: Keep the queue rows, the member rows and the reference load with rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1019-APP, -CON, -DB) and place the gate in rwb-access as POST and GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/queue-file-checks, with Reference data C for the check and R for the read; check the queue sheet only and pass a member sheet to the owner untouched; read DF-WRK-007 and DF-WRK-008 as capacity_cap and overflow_queue_code; read the cap maximum from the owner's parameters contract with the version in force; name the seven finding codes in the contract document only; write the acceptance entry with the code the owner's reference-load records and with no case id; and leave the rule-version operations of the legacy Endpoints table to RWB-AD-011 and RWB-AD-012.

title: The contract document of the queue-file check has no source schemas, no source finding codes and no source right for the approval
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-014); Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3 (A2.3, AC-EXC-P4-003-01, AC-EXC-P4-003-02); Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3 (T6.1, T6.2, T-A.1); P4 context pack
description: (a) No source document declares a schema for a queue file check, a finding, a check record or a check answer, so the four schemas, the field types and the finding shape are written by this run; (b) the seven finding codes and their severities are not source values; (c) the two operation paths are not in the ownership rows or in the API specification, and the exact path and shape of the five consumed owner operations are the owner's contract's, not this document's; (d) TSD P4 T6.1 grants no A letter in Reference data while the legacy permission row gives the approval the A letter of Rules and parameters to RW-RISK, so the right of the approval cannot be declared in this document and stays with the owner; (e) the idempotency key is declared on the reference-load family in TSD T-A.1 and is not declared for a check operation, so its reuse rule is written here; (f) the decision code of the acceptance entry and the exact message key of the 409 conflict are not stated.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T6.1 (rows for RW-COE, RW-REFADM, RW-RISK, RW-SECADM), T6.2, T-A.1 (API-P4-005 and API-P4-006 declare an Idempotency-Key header); FSD P4 v3 AC-P4-003-01, AC-EXC-P4-003-01, AC-EXC-P4-003-02; legacy RWB-AD-014 Permission checks and Validation and messages tables; P4 context pack REST operations provided (4).
proposed: Publish the four schemas, the seven Error finding codes, the 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 answers and the envelope mapping in one OpenAPI 3.1 document on base /api/recovery/access/v1; declare Reference data C and R on the two operations and leave the approval right with rwb-case; declare the Idempotency-Key header with a 200 replay and a 409 on a different file; and keep the document additive within v1.
